errors.evidence_quote: The number of sections created by the dotted line is equal to the number of times it intersects the colored lines.
errors.description: The model fundamentally misunderstands how line intersections divide segments. It incorrectly equates the number of intersections with the number of resulting sections, ignoring the basic geometric principle that each intersection on a continuous line adds one more section (i.e., n intersections → n+1 sections per line). This misunderstanding directly causes the model to undercount the total sections.

analysis_result.analysis: The model failed due to a combination of flawed premises and incorrect geometric reasoning. It assumed each rope was cut only once, ignoring multiple crossings per rope, and then incorrectly equated intersection counts with section counts, failing to apply the basic rule that n cuts create n+1 sections per line. These reasoning errors, not perceptual misidentifications, caused the model to output 6 instead of the correct 16.
